name: IFNA
description: IFNA returns a specified value when a formula results in the #N/A error, and otherwise returns the formula's own result. It catches only #N/A, not other errors.
tldr: Replaces #N/A errors with a fallback value.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The expression, formula, or cell to evaluate.

parameters.name: value_if_na
parameters.description: The value returned if value evaluates to #N/A.

basicExample.explanation: When the lookup finds no match it returns #N/A, which IFNA replaces with "Not found".

advancedExamples.title: Return zero instead of #N/A
advancedExamples.description: Use a numeric fallback for math
advancedExamples.explanation: This lets downstream math proceed without breaking on #N/A.

advancedExamples.title: IFNA vs IFERROR
advancedExamples.explanation: Because the error is #DIV/0! (not #N/A), IFNA does not catch it and the error passes through.

howItWorks: IFNA evaluates value first; if the result is the #N/A error it returns value_if_na, otherwise it returns the original result. It deliberately ignores all other error types.

howToSteps.name: Write the formula
howToSteps.text: Place the expression that might return #N/A as the first argument.

howToSteps.name: Add the fallback
howToSteps.text: Provide the value to show when #N/A occurs.

limitations: Only catches #N/A; use IFERROR to catch all error types.
If value_if_na is itself an error, that error is returned.

commonErrors.cause: IFNA only handles #N/A, so #VALUE!, #DIV/0!, etc. pass through.
commonErrors.fix: Use IFERROR if you need to catch every error type.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: IFNA works identically in Google Sheets, catching only #N/A.

faq.question: IFNA vs IFERROR?
faq.answer: IFNA catches only #N/A; IFERROR catches all error types. IFNA is safer when you only expect missing values.

faq.question: What happens to non-#N/A errors?
faq.answer: They are returned unchanged, not replaced.
